newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Speculation swirls around Waltons, Bidvest.
newsitem.headline: Speculation swirls around Waltons, Bidvest.

text.p: Speculation boosted shares prices in South African firms Pepkor, Waltons and Bidvest on Tuesday following a set of cautionary announcements by the firms.
The rumour mill has centred on the possible sale by Pepkor of its majority stake in struggling stationary company Waltons to industrial holding firm Bidvest.
In early trade Pepkor was up 35 cents to to 25.25 rand, Waltons hit a new year high of 820 cents before losing all the gains to be unchanged at 800 cents and Bidvest added five cents to 31.90 rand.

Analysts said the cautionaries -- one which covers Pepkor, Waltons Stationary Co Ltd and Walton Consolidated Investment Holdings Ltd, and the other the Bidvest Group Ltd and Bid Corp Ltd -- were likely to be linked.
"Almost definitely (they are linked). There have been such strong market rumours before...the odds are they are talking," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.
The analyst said one possible sticking point could be that Pepkor would be unwilling to sell its stake at less than the eight rand a share it paid for Waltons.
"Pepkor will not want to exit at below eight rand. And Bidvest is known not to be a big payer," he said.
In the year to February 28, Waltons' headline earnings slumped to 50.0 cents a share from 69.4 cents before.

It said at the time that the causes of the poor performance had been identified and a planned strategy had been put in place to restructure management, rationalise operations and improve financial reporting.
